.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:747:name: skill-creator
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:748:description: Guide for creating effective skills. This skill should be used when users want to create a new skill (or update an existing skill) that extends Codex's capabilities with specialized knowledge, workflows, or tool integrations.
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:750:  short-description: Create or update a skill
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:755:This skill provides guidance for creating effective skills.
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:795:You may use subagents during iteration to validate whether a skill works on realistic tasks or whether a suspected problem is real. This is most useful when you want an independent pass on the skill's behavior, outputs, or failure modes after a revision.  Only do this when it is possible to start new subagents.
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:797:When using subagents for validation, treat that as an evaluation surface. The goal is to learn whether the skill generalizes, not whether another agent can reconstruct the answer from leaked context.
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:803:Every skill consists of a required SKILL.md file and optional bundled resources:
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:806:skill-name/
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:813:│   └── openai.yaml - UI metadata for skill lists and chips
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:824:- **Frontmatter** (YAML): Contains `name` and `description` fields. These are the only fields that Codex reads to determine when the skill gets used, thus it is very important to be clear and comprehensive in describing what the skill is, and when it should be used.
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:825:- **Body** (Markdown): Instructions and guidance for using the skill. Only loaded AFTER the skill triggers (if at all).
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:829:- UI-facing metadata for skill lists and chips
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:831:- Create: human-facing `display_name`, `short_description`, and `default_prompt` by reading the skill
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:832:- Generate deterministically by passing the values as `--interface key=value` to `scripts/generate_openai_yaml.py` or `scripts/init_skill.py`
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:857:- **Avoid duplication**: Information should live in either SKILL.md or references files, not both. Prefer references files for detailed information unless it's truly core to the skill—this keeps SKILL.md lean while making information discoverable without hogging the context window. Keep only essential procedural instructions and workflow guidance in SKILL.md; move detailed reference material, schemas, and examples to references files.
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:863:- **When to include**: When the skill needs files that will be used in the final output
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:870:A skill should only contain essential files that directly support its functionality. Do NOT create extraneous documentation or auxiliary files, including:
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:878:The skill should only contain the information needed for an AI agent to do the job at hand. It should not contain auxiliary context about the process that went into creating it, setup and testing procedures, user-facing documentation, etc. Creating additional documentation files just adds clutter and confusion.
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:885:2. **SKILL.md body** - When skill triggers (<5k words)
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:890:Keep SKILL.md body to the essentials and under 500 lines to minimize context bloat. Split content into separate files when approaching this limit. When splitting out content into other files, it is very important to reference them from SKILL.md and describe clearly when to read them, to ensure the reader of the skill knows they exist and when to use them.
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:892:**Key principle:** When a skill supports multiple variations, frameworks, or options, keep only the core workflow and selection guidance in SKILL.md. Move variant-specific details (patterns, examples, configuration) into separate reference files.
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:918:bigquery-skill/
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:929:Similarly, for skills supporting multiple frameworks or variants, organize by variant:
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:972:1. Understand the skill with concrete examples
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:973:2. Plan reusable skill contents (scripts, references, assets)
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:974:3. Initialize the skill (run init_skill.py)
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:975:4. Edit the skill (implement resources and write SKILL.md)
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:976:5. Validate the skill (run quick_validate.py)
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:977:6. Iterate based on real usage and forward-test complex skills.
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:987:- Name the skill folder exactly after the skill name.
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:991:Skip this step only when the skill's usage patterns are already clearly understood. It remains valuable even when working with an existing skill.
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:993:To create an effective skill, clearly understand concrete examples of how the skill will be used. This understanding can come from either direct user examples or generated examples that are validated with user feedback.
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:995:For example, when building an image-editor skill, relevant questions include:
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:997:- "What functionality should the image-editor skill support? Editing, rotating, anything else?"
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:998:- "Can you give some examples of how this skill would be used?"
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:999:- "I can imagine users asking for things like 'Remove the red-eye from this image' or 'Rotate this image'. Are there other ways you imagine this skill being used?"
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:1000:- "What would a user say that should trigger this skill?"
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:1001:- "Where should I create this skill? If you do not have a preference, I will place it in `$CODEX_HOME/skills` (or `~/.codex/skills` when `CODEX_HOME` is unset) so Codex can discover it automatically."
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:1005:Conclude this step when there is a clear sense of the functionality the skill should support.

.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:1035:  default_prompt: "Optional surrounding prompt to use the skill with"
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:1055:- For `interface.default_prompt`: generate a helpful, short (typically 1 sentence) example starting prompt based on the skill. It must explicitly mention the skill as `$skill-name` (e.g., "Use $skill-name-here to draft a concise weekly status update.").
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:1057:- `interface.display_name`: Human-facing title shown in UI skill lists and chips.
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:1059:- `interface.icon_small`: Path to a small icon asset (relative to skill dir). Default to `./assets/` and place icons in the skill's `assets/` folder.
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:1060:- `interface.icon_large`: Path to a larger logo asset (relative to skill dir). Default to `./assets/` and place icons in the skill's `assets/` folder.
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:1062:- `interface.default_prompt`: Default prompt snippet inserted when invoking the skill.
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:1068:- `policy.allow_implicit_invocation`: When false, the skill is not injected into
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:1069:  the model context by default, but can still be invoked explicitly via `$skill`.

.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:1111:To turn concrete examples into an effective skill, analyze each example by:
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:1116:Example: When building a `pdf-editor` skill to handle queries like "Help me rotate this PDF," the analysis shows:
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:1119:2. A `scripts/rotate_pdf.py` script would be helpful to store in the skill
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:1121:Example: When designing a `frontend-webapp-builder` skill for queries like "Build me a todo app" or "Build me a dashboard to track my steps," the analysis shows:
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:1124:2. An `assets/hello-world/` template containing the boilerplate HTML/React project files would be helpful to store in the skill
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:1126:Example: When building a `big-query` skill to handle queries like "How many users have logged in today?" the analysis shows:
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:1129:2. A `references/schema.md` file documenting the table schemas would be helpful to store in the skill
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:1131:To establish the skill's contents, analyze each concrete example to create a list of the reusable resources to include: scripts, references, and assets.
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:1135:At this point, it is time to actually create the skill.
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:1137:Skip this step only if the skill being developed already exists. In this case, continue to the next step.
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:1139:Before running `init_skill.py`, ask where the user wants the skill created. If they do not specify a location, default to `$CODEX_HOME/skills`; when `CODEX_HOME` is unset, fall back to `~/.codex/skills` so the skill is auto-discovered.
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:1141:When creating a new skill from scratch, always run the `init_skill.py` script. The script conveniently generates a new template skill directory that automatically includes everything a skill requires, making the skill creation process much more efficient and reliable.
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:1146:scripts/init_skill.py <skill-name> --path <output-directory> [--resources scripts,references,assets] [--examples]
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:1152:scripts/init_skill.py my-skill --path "${CODEX_HOME:-$HOME/.codex}/skills"
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:1153:scripts/init_skill.py my-skill --path "${CODEX_HOME:-$HOME/.codex}/skills" --resources scripts,references
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:1154:scripts/init_skill.py my-skill --path ~/work/skills --resources scripts --examples
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:1159:- Creates the skill directory at the specified path
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:1167:Generate `display_name`, `short_description`, and `default_prompt` by reading the skill, then pass them as `--interface key=value` to `init_skill.py` or regenerate with:
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:1170:scripts/generate_openai_yaml.py <path/to/skill-folder> --interface key=value
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:1177:When editing the (newly-generated or existing) skill, remember that the skill is being created for another instance of Codex to use. Include information that would be beneficial and non-obvious to Codex. Consider what procedural knowledge, domain-specific details, or reusable assets would help another Codex instance execute these tasks more effectively.
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:1179:After substantial revisions, or if the skill is particularly tricky, you should use subagents to forward-test the skill on realistic tasks or artifacts. When doing so, pass the artifact under validation rather than your diagnosis of what is wrong, and keep the prompt generic enough that success depends on transferable reasoning rather than hidden ground truth.
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:1183:To begin implementation, start with the reusable resources identified above: `scripts/`, `references/`, and `assets/` files. Note that this step may require user input. For example, when implementing a `brand-guidelines` skill, the user may need to provide brand assets or templates to store in `assets/`, or documentation to store in `references/`.
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:1187:If you used `--examples`, delete any placeholder files that are not needed for the skill. Only create resource directories that are actually required.
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:1197:- `name`: The skill name
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:1198:- `description`: This is the primary triggering mechanism for your skill, and helps Codex understand when to use the skill.
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:1201:  - Example description for a `docx` skill: "Comprehensive document creation, editing, and analysis with support for tracked changes, comments, formatting preservation, and text extraction. Use when Codex needs to work with professional documents (.docx files) for: (1) Creating new documents, (2) Modifying or editing content, (3) Working with tracked changes, (4) Adding comments, or any other document tasks"
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:1207:Write instructions for using the skill and its bundled resources.
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:1211:Once development of the skill is complete, validate the skill folder to catch basic issues early:
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:1214:scripts/quick_validate.py <path/to/skill-folder>
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:1221:After testing the skill, you may detect the skill is complex enough that it requires forward-testing; or users may request improvements.
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:1223:User testing often this happens right after using the skill, with fresh context of how the skill performed.
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:1227:1. Use the skill on real tasks
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:1235:To forward-test, launch subagents as a way to stress test the skill with minimal context.
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:1236:Subagents should *not* know that they are being asked to test the skill.  They should be treated as
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:1238:  `Use $skill-x at /path/to/skill-x to solve problem y`
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:1240:  `Review the skill at /path/to/skill-x; pretend a user asks you to...`
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:1254:   - pass the skill, and a request in a similar way the user would.

.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:1572:description: Turn one product analysis card, implementation plan, UX analysis, or equivalent planning artifact into a complete screen-content plan for future visual mockups. Use when Codex needs to determine which screens are needed, what each screen must contain, what product data and states each screen requires, and what information is still missing before a separate mockup-generation skill begins. Do not use for generating visual mockups, styling systems, image assets, or implementation code.
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:1581:This skill is the first step in a two-skill workflow:
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:1583:1. This skill defines screen scope, content, data, states, reuse constraints, and unresolved blockers.
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:1584:2. A later visual mockup skill turns the plan into mockups.
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:1610:4. **Map planned behavior.** Use the provided implementation or product plan to identify workflows, states, roles, data entities, edge cases, failure modes, and permission differences that need screen coverage.
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:1614:8. **Prepare the handoff.** End with a clean handoff note for the later visual mockup skill, without doing visual design work.
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:1633:Do not ask for visual style details such as color palette, typography, illustration direction, spacing, motion, or high-fidelity layout preferences. Those belong to the later mockup creation skill.
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:1726:- Map the screen back to source requirements, workflows, implementation plan items, constraints, or acceptance criteria.
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:1751:- Which existing UI patterns the mockup skill must respect.
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:1763:- The output gives enough detail for a later visual mockup skill to work without rediscovering product intent.

.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2109:description: Turn one product analysis card, implementation plan, UX analysis, or equivalent planning artifact into a complete screen-content plan for future visual mockups. Use when Codex needs to determine which screens are needed, what each screen must contain, what product data and states each screen requires, and what information is still missing before a separate mockup-generation skill begins. Do not use for generating visual mockups, styling systems, image assets, or implementation code.
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2126:This skill is the first step in a two-skill workflow:
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2128:1. This skill defines screen scope, content, data, states, reuse constraints, and unresolved blockers.
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2129:2. A later visual mockup skill turns the plan into mockups.
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2155:4. **Map planned behavior.** Use the provided implementation or product plan to identify workflows, states, roles, data entities, edge cases, failure modes, and permission differences that need screen coverage.
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2159:8. **Prepare the handoff.** End with a clean handoff note for the later visual mockup skill, without doing visual design work.
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2178:Do not ask for visual style details such as color palette, typography, illustration direction, spacing, motion, or high-fidelity layout preferences. Those belong to the later mockup creation skill.

.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2331:Result type: Codex skill definition for turning one analysis card into a complete screen-content plan for later visual mockup creation.
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2333:Recommended skill name: `screen-content-planner`

.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2346:description: Turn one product analysis card, implementation plan, UX analysis, or equivalent planning artifact into a complete screen-content plan for future visual mockups. Use when Codex needs to determine which screens are needed, what each screen must contain, what product data and states each screen requires, and what information is still missing before a separate mockup-generation skill begins. Do not use for generating visual mockups, styling systems, image assets, or implementation code.
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2355:This skill is the first step in a two-skill workflow:
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2357:1. This skill defines screen scope, content, data, states, reuse constraints, and unresolved blockers.
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2358:2. A later visual mockup skill turns the plan into mockups.
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2384:4. **Map planned behavior.** Use the provided implementation or product plan to identify workflows, states, roles, data entities, edge cases, failure modes, and permission differences that need screen coverage.
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2388:8. **Prepare the handoff.** End with a clean handoff note for the later visual mockup skill, without doing visual design work.
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2407:Do not ask for visual style details such as color palette, typography, illustration direction, spacing, motion, or high-fidelity layout preferences. Those belong to the later mockup creation skill.

.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2604:name: skill-creator
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2605:description: Guide for creating effective skills. This skill should be used when users want to create a new skill (or update an existing skill) that extends Codex's capabilities with specialized knowledge, workflows, or tool integrations.
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2607:  short-description: Create or update a skill
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2620:This skill provides guidance for creating effective skills.
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2660:You may use subagents during iteration to validate whether a skill works on realistic tasks or whether a suspected problem is real. This is most useful when you want an independent pass on the skill's behavior, outputs, or failure modes after a revision.  Only do this when it is possible to start new subagents.
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2662:When using subagents for validation, treat that as an evaluation surface. The goal is to learn whether the skill generalizes, not whether another agent can reconstruct the answer from leaked context.
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2668:Every skill consists of a required SKILL.md file and optional bundled resources:
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2671:skill-name/
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2678:│   └── openai.yaml - UI metadata for skill lists and chips
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2689:- **Frontmatter** (YAML): Contains `name` and `description` fields. These are the only fields that Codex reads to determine when the skill gets used, thus it is very important to be clear and comprehensive in describing what the skill is, and when it should be used.
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2690:- **Body** (Markdown): Instructions and guidance for using the skill. Only loaded AFTER the skill triggers (if at all).
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2694:- UI-facing metadata for skill lists and chips
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2696:- Create: human-facing `display_name`, `short_description`, and `default_prompt` by reading the skill
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2697:- Generate deterministically by passing the values as `--interface key=value` to `scripts/generate_openai_yaml.py` or `scripts/init_skill.py`
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2722:- **Avoid duplication**: Information should live in either SKILL.md or references files, not both. Prefer references files for detailed information unless it's truly core to the skill—this keeps SKILL.md lean while making information discoverable without hogging the context window. Keep only essential procedural instructions and workflow guidance in SKILL.md; move detailed reference material, schemas, and examples to references files.
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2728:- **When to include**: When the skill needs files that will be used in the final output
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2735:A skill should only contain essential files that directly support its functionality. Do NOT create extraneous documentation or auxiliary files, including:
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2743:The skill should only contain the information needed for an AI agent to do the job at hand. It should not contain auxiliary context about the process that went into creating it, setup and testing procedures, user-facing documentation, etc. Creating additional documentation files just adds clutter and confusion.
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2750:2. **SKILL.md body** - When skill triggers (<5k words)
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2755:Keep SKILL.md body to the essentials and under 500 lines to minimize context bloat. Split content into separate files when approaching this limit. When splitting out content into other files, it is very important to reference them from SKILL.md and describe clearly when to read them, to ensure the reader of the skill knows they exist and when to use them.
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2757:**Key principle:** When a skill supports multiple variations, frameworks, or options, keep only the core workflow and selection guidance in SKILL.md. Move variant-specific details (patterns, examples, configuration) into separate reference files.
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2783:bigquery-skill/
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2794:Similarly, for skills supporting multiple frameworks or variants, organize by variant:
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2837:1. Understand the skill with concrete examples
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2838:2. Plan reusable skill contents (scripts, references, assets)
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2839:3. Initialize the skill (run init_skill.py)
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2840:4. Edit the skill (implement resources and write SKILL.md)
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2841:5. Validate the skill (run quick_validate.py)
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2842:6. Iterate based on real usage and forward-test complex skills.
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2852:- Name the skill folder exactly after the skill name.
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2856:Skip this step only when the skill's usage patterns are already clearly understood. It remains valuable even when working with an existing skill.
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2858:To create an effective skill, clearly understand concrete examples of how the skill will be used. This understanding can come from either direct user examples or generated examples that are validated with user feedback.
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2860:For example, when building an image-editor skill, relevant questions include:
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2862:- "What functionality should the image-editor skill support? Editing, rotating, anything else?"
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2863:- "Can you give some examples of how this skill would be used?"
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2864:- "I can imagine users asking for things like 'Remove the red-eye from this image' or 'Rotate this image'. Are there other ways you imagine this skill being used?"
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2865:- "What would a user say that should trigger this skill?"
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2866:- "Where should I create this skill? If you do not have a preference, I will place it in `$CODEX_HOME/skills` (or `~/.codex/skills` when `CODEX_HOME` is unset) so Codex can discover it automatically."
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2870:Conclude this step when there is a clear sense of the functionality the skill should support.
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2874:To turn concrete examples into an effective skill, analyze each example by:
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2879:Example: When building a `pdf-editor` skill to handle queries like "Help me rotate this PDF," the analysis shows:
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2882:2. A `scripts/rotate_pdf.py` script would be helpful to store in the skill
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2884:Example: When designing a `frontend-webapp-builder` skill for queries like "Build me a todo app" or "Build me a dashboard to track my steps," the analysis shows:
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2887:2. An `assets/hello-world/` template containing the boilerplate HTML/React project files would be helpful to store in the skill
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2889:Example: When building a `big-query` skill to handle queries like "How many users have logged in today?" the analysis shows:
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2892:2. A `references/schema.md` file documenting the table schemas would be helpful to store in the skill
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2894:To establish the skill's contents, analyze each concrete example to create a list of the reusable resources to include: scripts, references, and assets.
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2898:At this point, it is time to actually create the skill.
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2900:Skip this step only if the skill being developed already exists. In this case, continue to the next step.
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2902:Before running `init_skill.py`, ask where the user wants the skill created. If they do not specify a location, default to `$CODEX_HOME/skills`; when `CODEX_HOME` is unset, fall back to `~/.codex/skills` so the skill is auto-discovered.
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2904:When creating a new skill from scratch, always run the `init_skill.py` script. The script conveniently generates a new template skill directory that automatically includes everything a skill requires, making the skill creation process much more efficient and reliable.
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2909:scripts/init_skill.py <skill-name> --path <output-directory> [--resources scripts,references,assets] [--examples]
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2915:scripts/init_skill.py my-skill --path "${CODEX_HOME:-$HOME/.codex}/skills"
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2916:scripts/init_skill.py my-skill --path "${CODEX_HOME:-$HOME/.codex}/skills" --resources scripts,references
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2917:scripts/init_skill.py my-skill --path ~/work/skills --resources scripts --examples
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2922:- Creates the skill directory at the specified path
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2930:Generate `display_name`, `short_description`, and `default_prompt` by reading the skill, then pass them as `--interface key=value` to `init_skill.py` or regenerate with:
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2933:scripts/generate_openai_yaml.py <path/to/skill-folder> --interface key=value
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2940:When editing the (newly-generated or existing) skill, remember that the skill is being created for another instance of Codex to use. Include information that would be beneficial and non-obvious to Codex. Consider what procedural knowledge, domain-specific details, or reusable assets would help another Codex instance execute these tasks more effectively.
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2942:After substantial revisions, or if the skill is particularly tricky, you should use subagents to forward-test the skill on realistic tasks or artifacts. When doing so, pass the artifact under validation rather than your diagnosis of what is wrong, and keep the prompt generic enough that success depends on transferable reasoning rather than hidden ground truth.
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2946:To begin implementation, start with the reusable resources identified above: `scripts/`, `references/`, and `assets/` files. Note that this step may require user input. For example, when implementing a `brand-guidelines` skill, the user may need to provide brand assets or templates to store in `assets/`, or documentation to store in `references/`.
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2950:If you used `--examples`, delete any placeholder files that are not needed for the skill. Only create resource directories that are actually required.
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2960:- `name`: The skill name
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2961:- `description`: This is the primary triggering mechanism for your skill, and helps Codex understand when to use the skill.
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2964:  - Example description for a `docx` skill: "Comprehensive document creation, editing, and analysis with support for tracked changes, comments, formatting preservation, and text extraction. Use when Codex needs to work with professional documents (.docx files) for: (1) Creating new documents, (2) Modifying or editing content, (3) Working with tracked changes, (4) Adding comments, or any other document tasks"
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2970:Write instructions for using the skill and its bundled resources.
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2974:Once development of the skill is complete, validate the skill folder to catch basic issues early:
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2977:scripts/quick_validate.py <path/to/skill-folder>
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2984:After testing the skill, you may detect the skill is complex enough that it requires forward-testing; or users may request improvements.
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2986:User testing often this happens right after using the skill, with fresh context of how the skill performed.
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2990:1. Use the skill on real tasks
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2998:To forward-test, launch subagents as a way to stress test the skill with minimal context.
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2999:Subagents should *not* know that they are being asked to test the skill.  They should be treated as

.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:3065:description: Turn one product analysis card, implementation plan, UX analysis, or equivalent planning artifact into a complete screen-content plan for future visual mockups. Use when Codex needs to determine which screens are needed, what each screen must contain, what app language, platform format, product wording, data, states, and missing information are required before a separate mockup-generation skill begins. Do not use for generating visual mockups, styling systems, image assets, or implementation code.
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:3074:This skill is the first step in a two-skill workflow:
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:3076:1. This skill defines screen scope, content, data, states, reuse constraints, and unresolved blockers.
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:3077:2. A later visual mockup skill turns the plan into mockups.
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:3107:5. **Map planned behavior.** Use the provided implementation or product plan to identify workflows, states, roles, data entities, edge cases, failure modes, and permission differences that need screen coverage.
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:3110:8. **Review wording for production readiness.** Ensure labels, headings, empty states, errors, CTAs, helper text, and status messages are written for end users, not developers or implementation teams.
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:3112:10. **Prepare the handoff.** End with a clean handoff note for the later visual mockup skill, without doing visual design work.
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:3134:Do not ask for visual style details such as color palette, typography, illustration direction, spacing, motion, or high-fidelity layout preferences. Those belong to the later mockup creation skill.
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:3142:Use wording that a real end user can understand in the application language. Avoid implementation wording, internal team shorthand, database names, component names, raw enum values, route names, debug labels, placeholder text, and developer instructions unless the product itself is for developers and the source explicitly requires that vocabulary.
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:3230:- Ensure every wording item is end-user-facing, in the application language, and free of development or implementation jargon.
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:3254:- Map the screen back to source requirements, workflows, implementation plan items, constraints, or acceptance criteria.
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:3282:- Which existing UI patterns the mockup skill must respect.
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:3283:- Which application language and platform format the mockup skill must use.
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:3284:- Which wording requirements or draft copy the mockup skill must preserve.
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:3295:- User-facing wording is production-ready, in the application language, and free of development jargon, internal shorthand, raw technical states, placeholders, and implementation labels.
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:3298:- The output gives enough detail for a later visual mockup skill to work without rediscovering product intent.

.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:4:Ici, on a besoin de créer un skill qui va prendre le résultat du skill qu'on avait créé qui s'appelle Screen Content Planner, corrigé d'une bloat analysis éventuellement. En tout cas, ça prend une description de skill et enfin, ça prend une description de screen, pardon, et ça les transforme en mock-up visuel. Ce que ça fait, c'est que si jamais c'est une technologie web, on les fait directement, en fait, quoi qu'il arrive, en fait, on les fait en HTML et CSS. Et il faut bien que le skill, avant de générer les screens, il fasse une analyse complète des styles avec les couleurs, les border radius. En fait, il faut réutiliser ce qu'il y a dans Frontend skill pour pouvoir faire une analyse du design qu'on a dans l'application pour que les mock-ups, ils soient cohérents avec ce qu'on a déjà dans l'application. Et ensuite, ce qu'il faut que ça fasse, c'est que ça, du coup, ça génère les fichiers HTML et CSS, le CSS séparé du HTML à chaque fois. Chaque screen, il est dans son fichier HTML et chaque fichier HTML, il a son fichier CSS. Et ensuite, ce qu'on fait, c'est qu'on render avec le format d'image correct qui correspond à ce qu'on est en train de faire. Donc, par exemple, si c'est une application mobile en mode portrait, il faut qu'on fasse un render dans du browser en 9 16e et qu'on fasse ensuite une capture d'image et qu'on construise un carrousel dans la carte pour pouvoir montrer tous les mock-ups dans un carrousel. C'est aussi important que dans le skill, il y ait les règles de formatting qu'on a pour décision OS. Et ça veut dire qu'à chaque fois, je veux que les outputs soient créés avec les règles de formatting. Donc, ça veut dire que nos règles de formatting, il faut qu'on les ajoute à chaque skill qui est une tâche que tu dois faire alternative. Non, non, oublie cette tâche, je veux la faire moi-même. En tout cas, dans le skill que tu crées, il faudra mettre les règles de formatting et les règles de formatting, du coup, c'est les règles de formatting des cartes. C'est-à-dire que quand output du markdown, il faut que les titres, ils aient une lettre, que les sous-titres, ils aient une lettre un numéro, que les bullet points, elles aient des numéros, il faut que chaque section, elle soit séparée par un HR et il faut qu'il y ait du bold et des bactics.

.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:257:description: Guide for creating effective skills. This skill should be used when users want to create a new skill (or update an existing skill) that extends Codex's capabilities with specialized knowledge, workflows, or tool integrations.
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:259:  short-description: Create or update a skill
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:264:This skill provides guidance for creating effective skills.
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:304:You may use subagents during iteration to validate whether a skill works on realistic tasks or whether a suspected problem is real. This is most useful when you want an independent pass on the skill's behavior, outputs, or failure modes after a revision.  Only do this when it is possible to start new subagents.
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:306:When using subagents for validation, treat that as an evaluation surface. The goal is to learn whether the skill generalizes, not whether another agent can reconstruct the answer from leaked context.
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:312:Every skill consists of a required SKILL.md file and optional bundled resources:
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:315:skill-name/
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:322:│   └── openai.yaml - UI metadata for skill lists and chips
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:333:- **Frontmatter** (YAML): Contains `name` and `description` fields. These are the only fields that Codex reads to determine when the skill gets used, thus it is very important to be clear and comprehensive in describing what the skill is, and when it should be used.
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:334:- **Body** (Markdown): Instructions and guidance for using the skill. Only loaded AFTER the skill triggers (if at all).
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:338:- UI-facing metadata for skill lists and chips
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:340:- Create: human-facing `display_name`, `short_description`, and `default_prompt` by reading the skill
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:341:- Generate deterministically by passing the values as `--interface key=value` to `scripts/generate_openai_yaml.py` or `scripts/init_skill.py`
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:366:- **Avoid duplication**: Information should live in either SKILL.md or references files, not both. Prefer references files for detailed information unless it's truly core to the skill—this keeps SKILL.md lean while making information discoverable without hogging the context window. Keep only essential procedural instructions and workflow guidance in SKILL.md; move detailed reference material, schemas, and examples to references files.
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:372:- **When to include**: When the skill needs files that will be used in the final output
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:379:A skill should only contain essential files that directly support its functionality. Do NOT create extraneous documentation or auxiliary files, including:
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:387:The skill should only contain the information needed for an AI agent to do the job at hand. It should not contain auxiliary context about the process that went into creating it, setup and testing procedures, user-facing documentation, etc. Creating additional documentation files just adds clutter and confusion.
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:394:2. **SKILL.md body** - When skill triggers (<5k words)
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:399:Keep SKILL.md body to the essentials and under 500 lines to minimize context bloat. Split content into separate files when approaching this limit. When splitting out content into other files, it is very important to reference them from SKILL.md and describe clearly when to read them, to ensure the reader of the skill knows they exist and when to use them.
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:401:**Key principle:** When a skill supports multiple variations, frameworks, or options, keep only the core workflow and selection guidance in SKILL.md. Move variant-specific details (patterns, examples, configuration) into separate reference files.
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:427:bigquery-skill/
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:438:Similarly, for skills supporting multiple frameworks or variants, organize by variant:
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:481:1. Understand the skill with concrete examples
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:482:2. Plan reusable skill contents (scripts, references, assets)
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:483:3. Initialize the skill (run init_skill.py)
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:484:4. Edit the skill (implement resources and write SKILL.md)
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:485:5. Validate the skill (run quick_validate.py)
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:486:6. Iterate based on real usage and forward-test complex skills.
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:496:- Name the skill folder exactly after the skill name.
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:500:Skip this step only when the skill's usage patterns are already clearly understood. It remains valuable even when working with an existing skill.
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:502:To create an effective skill, clearly understand concrete examples of how the skill will be used. This understanding can come from either direct user examples or generated examples that are validated with user feedback.
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:504:For example, when building an image-editor skill, relevant questions include:
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:506:- "What functionality should the image-editor skill support? Editing, rotating, anything else?"
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:507:- "Can you give some examples of how this skill would be used?"
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:508:- "I can imagine users asking for things like 'Remove the red-eye from this image' or 'Rotate this image'. Are there other ways you imagine this skill being used?"
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:509:- "What would a user say that should trigger this skill?"
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:510:- "Where should I create this skill? If you do not have a preference, I will place it in `$CODEX_HOME/skills` (or `~/.codex/skills` when `CODEX_HOME` is unset) so Codex can discover it automatically."
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:514:Conclude this step when there is a clear sense of the functionality the skill should support.

.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:676:/home/jbb/dev/EditorBP/decision-os/.decision-os/cards/skills/card-1ed7edae-2bff-4f0e-a922-1bb57a0b6e93.md:5:3. **Workflow position:** This is the first skill in a two-skill workflow. Ce que ça fait, c'est que si jamais c'est une technologie web, on les fait directement, en fait, quoi qu'il arrive, en fait, on les fait en HTML et CSS. Et il faut bien que le skill, avant de générer les screens, il fasse une analyse complète des styles avec les couleurs, les border radius. En fait, il faut réutiliser ce qu'il y a dans Frontend skill pour pouvoir faire une analyse du design qu'on a dans l'application pour que les mock-ups, ils soient cohérents avec ce qu'on a déjà dans l'application. Et ensuite, ce qu'il faut que ça fasse, c'est que ça, du coup, ça génère les fichiers HTML et CSS, le CSS séparé du HTML à chaque fois. Chaque screen, il est dans son fichier HTML et chaque fichier HTML, il a son fichier CSS. Et ensuite, ce qu'on fait, c'est qu'on render avec le format d'image correct qui correspond à ce qu'on est en train de faire. Donc, par exemple, si c'est une application mobile en mode portrait, il faut qu'on fasse un render dans du browser en 9 16e et qu'on fasse ensuite une capture d'image et qu'on construise un carrousel dans la carte pour pouvoir montrer tous les mock-ups dans un carrousel. C'est aussi important que dans le skill, il y ait les règles de formatting qu'on a pour décision OS. Et ça veut dire qu'à chaque fois, je veux que les outputs soient créés avec les règles de formatting. Donc, ça veut dire que nos règles de formatting, il faut qu'on les ajoute à chaque skill qui est une tâche que tu dois faire alternative. Non, non, oublie cette tâche, je veux la faire moi-même. En tout cas, dans le skill que tu crées, il faudra mettre les règles de formatting et les règles de formatting, du coup, c'est les règles de formatting des cartes. C'est-à-dire que quand output du markdown, il faut que les titres, ils aient une lettre, que les sous-titres, ils aient une lettre un numéro, que les bullet points, elles aient des numéros, il faut que chaque section, elle soit séparée par un HR et il faut qu'il y ait du bold et des bactics.

.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:773:/home/jbb/dev/EditorBP/decision-os/.decision-os/threads/tasks-system/thread-card-codex-skill-1783443352880-df6faf0b.md:2384:    33	1. **Journeys.** A user opens a ledger route, reviews the canvas, selects or creates cards/zones/groups, edits geometry or content, opens the thread panel with `A`, writes or records notes, receives agent replies, reviews card media or report mockups, and can use CLI workflows for maintenance or agent treatment.
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:777:/home/jbb/dev/EditorBP/decision-os/.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-1ed7edae-2bff-4f0e-a922-1bb57a0b6e93.md:4:Ici, je veux que tu settes le goal de la carte et l'idée, c'est de créer un skill pour pouvoir faire des mockups qui sont toujours en rapport avec la tech stack qu'on utilise, qui sont en rapport avec tous les screens qu'on a déjà et toutes les features qu'on a déjà. Et ça partira systématiquement d'une carte d'analyse. Donc, normalement, il y aura le contexte suffisant, enfin, d'une carte d'un contenu, c'est-à-dire qu'on donne le contenu de l'analyse, de la stack, de machin, de ce qu'il faut faire avec un plan assez précis. Et ensuite, ça, c'est censé comprendre combien, peut-être poser des questions, vérifier combien il doit y avoir de screens. Et une fois qu'on a bien compris combien il y avait de screens, en fait, il faut bien définir le contenu de tous les screens. Ouais, en fait, on fait deux skills. Le premier skill, c'est un skill qui d'abord définit le contenu des screens et s'assure qu'il y a toute la donnée nécessaire. Et l'autre skill de création des mocks visuels, on le fera dans un autre temps.
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:778:/home/jbb/dev/EditorBP/decision-os/.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-1ed7edae-2bff-4f0e-a922-1bb57a0b6e93.md:11:I rewrote the card goal as a specification for the first skill only: a screen-content planning skill that starts from an analysis card, checks stack and existing-product context, determines or clarifies the needed screen count, and defines the content requirements for every screen.
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:779:/home/jbb/dev/EditorBP/decision-os/.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-1ed7edae-2bff-4f0e-a922-1bb57a0b6e93.md:13:I kept the later visual mockup creation skill explicitly out of scope so this card can serve as the handoff contract for that future skill.
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:780:/home/jbb/dev/EditorBP/decision-os/.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-1ed7edae-2bff-4f0e-a922-1bb57a0b6e93.md:178:Ici, je veux que tu settes le goal de la carte et l'idée, c'est de créer un skill pour pouvoir faire des mockups qui sont toujours en rapport avec la tech stack qu'on utilise, qui sont en rapport avec tous les screens qu'on a déjà et toutes les features qu'on a déjà. Et ça partira systématiquement d'une carte d'analyse. Donc, normalement, il y aura le contexte suffisant, enfin, d'une carte d'un contenu, c'est-à-dire qu'on donne le contenu de l'analyse, de la stack, de machin, de ce qu'il faut faire avec un plan assez précis. Et ensuite, ça, c'est censé comprendre combien, peut-être poser des questions, vérifier combien il doit y avoir de screens. Et une fois qu'on a bien compris combien il y avait de screens, en fait, il faut bien définir le contenu de tous les screens. Ouais, en fait, on fait deux skills. Le premier skill, c'est un skill qui d'abord définit le contenu des screens et s'assure qu'il y a toute la donnée nécessaire. Et l'autre skill de création des mocks visuels, on le fera dans un autre temps.
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:781:/home/jbb/dev/EditorBP/decision-os/.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-1ed7edae-2bff-4f0e-a922-1bb57a0b6e93.md:200:The thread request is to define the card goal, not to implement the visual mockup generator yet. .decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:1041:To turn concrete examples into an effective skill, analyze each example by:
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:1046:Example: When building a `pdf-editor` skill to handle queries like "Help me rotate this PDF," the analysis shows:
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:1049:2. A `scripts/rotate_pdf.py` script would be helpful to store in the skill
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:1051:Example: When designing a `frontend-webapp-builder` skill for queries like "Build me a todo app" or "Build me a dashboard to track my steps," the analysis shows:
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:1054:2. An `assets/hello-world/` template containing the boilerplate HTML/React project files would be helpful to store in the skill
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:1056:Example: When building a `big-query` skill to handle queries like "How many users have logged in today?" the analysis shows:
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:1059:2. A `references/schema.md` file documenting the table schemas would be helpful to store in the skill
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:1061:To establish the skill's contents, analyze each concrete example to create a list of the reusable resources to include: scripts, references, and assets.
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:1065:At this point, it is time to actually create the skill.
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:1067:Skip this step only if the skill being developed already exists. In this case, continue to the next step.
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:1069:Before running `init_skill.py`, ask where the user wants the skill created. If they do not specify a location, default to `$CODEX_HOME/skills`; when `CODEX_HOME` is unset, fall back to `~/.codex/skills` so the skill is auto-discovered.
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:1071:When creating a new skill from scratch, always run the `init_skill.py` script. The script conveniently generates a new template skill directory that automatically includes everything a skill requires, making the skill creation process much more efficient and reliable.
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:1076:scripts/init_skill.py <skill-name> --path <output-directory> [--resources scripts,references,assets] [--examples]
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:1082:scripts/init_skill.py my-skill --path "${CODEX_HOME:-$HOME/.codex}/skills"

.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:1089:- Creates the skill directory at the specified path
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:1097:Generate `display_name`, `short_description`, and `default_prompt` by reading the skill, then pass them as `--interface key=value` to `init_skill.py` or regenerate with:
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:1100:scripts/generate_openai_yaml.py <path/to/skill-folder> --interface key=value
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:1107:When editing the (newly-generated or existing) skill, remember that the skill is being created for another instance of Codex to use. Include information that would be beneficial and non-obvious to Codex. Consider what procedural knowledge, domain-specific details, or reusable assets would help another Codex instance execute these tasks more effectively.
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:1109:After substantial revisions, or if the skill is particularly tricky, you should use subagents to forward-test the skill on realistic tasks or artifacts. When doing so, pass the artifact under validation rather than your diagnosis of what is wrong, and keep the prompt generic enough that success depends on transferable reasoning rather than hidden ground truth.
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:1113:To begin implementation, start with the reusable resources identified above: `scripts/`, `references/`, and `assets/` files. Note that this step may require user input. For example, when implementing a `brand-guidelines` skill, the user may need to provide brand assets or templates to store in `assets/`, or documentation to store in `references/`.
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:1117:If you used `--examples`, delete any placeholder files that are not needed for the skill. Only create resource directories that are actually required.

.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:1153:User testing often this happens right after using the skill, with fresh context of how the skill performed.

.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:1217:description: Turn one product analysis card, implementation plan, UX analysis, or equivalent planning artifact into a complete screen-content plan for future visual mockups. Use when Codex needs to determine which screens are needed, what each screen must contain, what product data and states each screen requires, and what information is still missing before a separate mockup-generation skill begins. Do not use for generating visual mockups, styling systems, image assets, or implementation code.
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:1226:This skill is the first step in a two-skill workflow:
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:1228:1. This skill defines screen scope, content, data, states, reuse constraints, and unresolved blockers.
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:1229:2. A later visual mockup skill turns the plan into mockups.
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:1255:4. **Map planned behavior.** Use the provided implementation or product plan to identify workflows, states, roles, data entities, edge cases, failure modes, and permission differences that need screen coverage.
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:1259:8. **Prepare the handoff.** End with a clean handoff note for the later visual mockup skill, without doing visual design work.
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:1278:Do not ask for visual style details such as color palette, typography, illustration direction, spacing, motion, or high-fidelity layout preferences. Those belong to the later mockup creation skill.
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:1371:- Map the screen back to source requirements, workflows, implementation plan items, constraints, or acceptance criteria.
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:1396:- Which existing UI patterns the mockup skill must respect.
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:1408:- The output gives enough detail for a later visual mockup skill to work without rediscovering product intent.

.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:1514:description: Create distinctive, production-grade frontend interfaces with high design quality. Use this skill when the user asks to build web components, pages, or applications. Generates creative, polished code that avoids generic AI aesthetics.
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:1518:This skill guides creation of distinctive, production-grade frontend interfaces that avoid generic "AI slop" aesthetics. Implement real working code with exceptional attention to aesthetic details and creative choices.
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:1543:- **Motion**: Use animations for effects and micro-interactions. Prioritize CSS-only solutions for HTML. Use Motion library for React when available. Focus on high-impact moments: one well-orchestrated page load with staggered reveals (animation-delay) creates more delight than scattered micro-interactions. Use scroll-triggering and hover states that surprise.
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:1551:**IMPORTANT**: Match implementation complexity to the aesthetic vision. Maximalist designs need elaborate code with extensive animations and effects. Minimalist or refined designs need restraint, precision, and careful attention to spacing, typography, and subtle details. Elegance comes from executing the vision well.

.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:1846:description: Convert a screen-content plan, UX plan, product analysis card, or equivalent screen description into visual mockups. .decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:1855:This skill follows `screen-content-planner`: consume its screen inventory, per-screen definitions, cross-screen coverage check, and handoff. .decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:2814:Ici, on a besoin de créer un skill qui va prendre le résultat du skill qu'on avait créé qui s'appelle Screen Content Planner, corrigé d'une bloat analysis éventuellement. En tout cas, ça prend une description de skill et enfin, ça prend une description de screen, pardon, et ça les transforme en mock-up visuel. Ce que ça fait, c'est que si jamais c'est une technologie web, on les fait directement, en fait, quoi qu'il arrive, en fait, on les fait en HTML et CSS. Et il faut bien que le skill, avant de générer les screens, il fasse une analyse complète des styles avec les couleurs, les border radius. En fait, il faut réutiliser ce qu'il y a dans Frontend skill pour pouvoir faire une analyse du design qu'on a dans l'application pour que les mock-ups, ils soient cohérents avec ce qu'on a déjà dans l'application. Et ensuite, ce qu'il faut que ça fasse, c'est que ça, du coup, ça génère les fichiers HTML et CSS, le CSS séparé du HTML à chaque fois. Chaque screen, il est dans son fichier HTML et chaque fichier HTML, il a son fichier CSS. Et ensuite, ce qu'on fait, c'est qu'on render avec le format d'image correct qui correspond à ce qu'on est en train de faire. Donc, par exemple, si c'est une application mobile en mode portrait, il faut qu'on fasse un render dans du browser en 9 16e et qu'on fasse ensuite une capture d'image et qu'on construise un carrousel dans la carte pour pouvoir montrer tous les mock-ups dans un carrousel. C'est aussi important que dans le skill, il y ait les règles de formatting qu'on a pour décision OS. Et ça veut dire qu'à chaque fois, je veux que les outputs soient créés avec les règles de formatting. Donc, ça veut dire que nos règles de formatting, il faut qu'on les ajoute à chaque skill qui est une tâche que tu dois faire alternative. Non, non, oublie cette tâche, je veux la faire moi-même. En tout cas, dans le skill que tu crées, il faudra mettre les règles de formatting et les règles de formatting, du coup, c'est les règles de formatting des cartes. C'est-à-dire que quand output du markdown, il faut que les titres, ils aient une lettre, que les sous-titres, ils aient une lettre un numéro, que les bullet points, elles aient des numéros, il faut que chaque section, elle soit séparée par un HR et il faut qu'il y ait du bold et des bactics.

.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:3033:Ici, on a besoin de créer un skill qui va prendre le résultat du skill qu'on avait créé qui s'appelle Screen Content Planner, corrigé d'une bloat analysis éventuellement. En tout cas, ça prend une description de skill et enfin, ça prend une description de screen, pardon, et ça les transforme en mock-up visuel. Ce que ça fait, c'est que si jamais c'est une technologie web, on les fait directement, en fait, quoi qu'il arrive, en fait, on les fait en HTML et CSS. Et il faut bien que le skill, avant de générer les screens, il fasse une analyse complète des styles avec les couleurs, les border radius. En fait, il faut réutiliser ce qu'il y a dans Frontend skill pour pouvoir faire une analyse du design qu'on a dans l'application pour que les mock-ups, ils soient cohérents avec ce qu'on a déjà dans l'application. Et ensuite, ce qu'il faut que ça fasse, c'est que ça, du coup, ça génère les fichiers HTML et CSS, le CSS séparé du HTML à chaque fois. Chaque screen, il est dans son fichier HTML et chaque fichier HTML, il a son fichier CSS. Et ensuite, ce qu'on fait, c'est qu'on render avec le format d'image correct qui correspond à ce qu'on est en train de faire. Donc, par exemple, si c'est une application mobile en mode portrait, il faut qu'on fasse un render dans du browser en 9 16e et qu'on fasse ensuite une capture d'image et qu'on construise un carrousel dans la carte pour pouvoir montrer tous les mock-ups dans un carrousel. C'est aussi important que dans le skill, il y ait les règles de formatting qu'on a pour décision OS. Et ça veut dire qu'à chaque fois, je veux que les outputs soient créés avec les règles de formatting. Donc, ça veut dire que nos règles de formatting, il faut qu'on les ajoute à chaque skill qui est une tâche que tu dois faire alternative. Non, non, oublie cette tâche, je veux la faire moi-même. En tout cas, dans le skill que tu crées, il faudra mettre les règles de formatting et les règles de formatting, du coup, c'est les règles de formatting des cartes. C'est-à-dire que quand output du markdown, il faut que les titres, ils aient une lettre, que les sous-titres, ils aient une lettre un numéro, que les bullet points, elles aient des numéros, il faut que chaque section, elle soit séparée par un HR et il faut qu'il y ait du bold et des bactics.
